children: Euro zone yields steadied on Wednesday as bond markets stabilised following hot US inflation data a day earlier that jolted Treasuries and spilled over into Europe.
US bond markets were closed on Wednesday for the Veterans Day holiday, reducing liquidity in the market and subduing global trading.
Germany's 10-year yield was last up 1 basis point at 3.32%. Yields move inversely to prices. (DE10YT=RR)
The benchmark yield rose 4 bps on Tuesday as 10-year US borrowing costs
jumped 12 bps following US inflation data that showed price pressures rose more than expected in October.
Traders added to their bets on US Federal Reserve rate hikes and now see a December increase as a certainty.
Given the importance of the US economy, the data also caused traders to nudge up their bets on a December hike from the European Central Bank, which is now seen as almost guaranteed.

Comments from European Central Bank chief economist Philip Lane to Bloomberg Television, in which he said that it would be "prudent" to raise rates in December if the data did not meaningfully change, added to the mounting wagers on a hike.
Germany's interest-rate-sensitive 2-year bond yield (DE2YT=RR) rose 2 bps on Wednesday to 3.10%, after rising 8 bps on Tuesday. (DE2YT=RR)
Analysts said it made sense for a knee-jerk reaction to the US data to fade in Europe.
"Markets are quick to translate tighter Fed policy into tighter ECB policy. But the reality is more complex," said Michiel Tukker, senior UK and euro zone rates strategist at ING.
"Both regions face very different inflation paths, whereby Europe is more exposed to energy prices and the US to AI-related growth."
He said a tight correlation between US and European rates is warranted if driven by oil as the common denominator, but less so if triggered by macroeconomic data.
And recent oil price moves have been pointing to lower yields. A sharp drop in oil prices has taken Brent crude to around its lowest since late August
after the US midterms delivered a rebuke to President Donald Trump and his war on Iran.
That has offered some relief to embattled French debt.
France's 10-year bond yield (FR10YT=RR) was up 1 bp at 4.80% after rising 7 bps on Tuesday.
The closely watched spread between French and German yields – a measure of the risk premium attached to France, which has jumped this year – was steady at 147 bps.
It rose to 178 bps in October, its highest since 2011 (DE10FR10=RR).
Spain's 10-year yields (ES10YT=R) also rose 1 bp, with markets shrugging off the first general strike by Spanish workers – driven by anger over housing – in 14 years.
Also on Wednesday, Germany sold €2.5 billion ($2.8 billion) of longer-dated bonds, with demand mixed.
